This report follows the structure of the VPAT® 2.5 (WCAG edition). It covers **Lumen 0.1.0** (web, desktop and mobile) against **WCAG 2.2** levels A and AA, and was last reviewed on **2026-11-10**. It is published again with every major release: `node scripts/acr.mjs --check` fails when the report's version and the app's differ.

## Summary

| Level | Supports | Partially supports | Does not support | Not applicable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 22 | 5 | 0 | 4 |
| AA | 16 | 6 | 0 | 2 |

## How it was evaluated

Automated: axe-core on six surfaces in Hebrew and English, light and dark (e2e/a11y.spec.ts); reflow at 320 and 640 px and forced colours (e2e/reflow.spec.ts); spoken announcements (e2e/sr-announce.spec.ts); unit tests of the focus trap, contrast and toasts. Manual: review of each criterion against the app's code and behaviour for this version.

## Level A

| Criterion | Status | Remarks |
|---|---|---|
| [1.1.1 Non-text Content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content) | Partially supports | Icons and icon buttons have text names (axe). Charts, diagrams, the canvas and maps drawn from note text are pictures: their alternative is the source text in the note, which is always one click away, but the picture itself has no text alternative. **Plan:** Give chart and diagram blocks a text summary (title, series, values) as their accessible name, and the canvas an outline of its shapes. (0.2.0) |
| [1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded) | Not applicable | Lumen's own interface has no prerecorded audio or video. Media in notes is the author's content. |
| [1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded) | Not applicable | No prerecorded media with sound in the interface. |
| [1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded) | Not applicable | No prerecorded video in the interface. |
| [1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships) | Supports | Dialogs, menus, the palette (combobox + listbox), tabs, tables and forms use native elements or ARIA roles with names. In the editor, the structure of the line under the cursor (heading level, task state, code block, quote) is spoken. |
| [1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/meaningful-sequence) | Supports | The reading order follows the DOM order in both directions; Hebrew and English runs are isolated so they read in their own direction. |
| [1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/sensory-characteristics) | Supports | Instructions name the control ("the Settings button", "⌘K"), never only its shape, colour or place. |
| [1.4.1 Use of Color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color) | Partially supports | Messages, errors and selections carry text or a named icon as well as colour (axe's colour rules pass on six surfaces). In the status bar, the sync and collaboration indicators show their state by icon and colour, with the words only in a tooltip. **Plan:** Status-bar indicators with a visible word ("Synced", "Offline") and an accessible name, translated (their tooltips are English-only today). (0.2.0) |
| [1.4.2 Audio Control](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-control) | Supports | Nothing plays sound on its own. Read-aloud starts on request and has a stop control. |
| [2.1.1 Keyboard](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard) | Partially supports | Every feature is a command in the palette, dialogs keep and return focus, the sidebar edge resizes with arrow keys. The canvas whiteboard (tldraw) and the map can be panned and zoomed with the keyboard, but drawing new shapes needs a pointer. **Plan:** Keyboard commands to add, move and connect shapes on the canvas. (0.2.0) |
| [2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap) | Supports | Tab in the editor indents (as in every code editor); pressing Escape and then Tab moves focus out (CodeMirror's behaviour). Dialogs release focus on Escape. |
| [2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts) | Supports | Global shortcuts use a modifier (⌘ / Ctrl / Alt). Single-key keys work only while a component has focus (lists, the calendar grid), or in Vim mode, which is off unless turned on. |
| [2.2.1 Timing Adjustable](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/timing-adjustable) | Supports | No task has a time limit. Notifications that go away on their own stay while the pointer is over them or focus is in them (fixed for this report), and every one has a close button. |
| [2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide) | Supports | No content moves or blinks for more than five seconds, except progress spinners while work runs. With the system's reduce-motion setting, animations stop. |
| [2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold) | Supports | Nothing flashes. |
| [2.4.1 Bypass Blocks](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/bypass-blocks) | Supports | A skip link jumps to the main content; landmarks name the regions. |
| [2.4.2 Page Titled](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/page-titled) | Supports | The page title names the app ("Lumen — Markdown, illuminated"). It does not yet change with the open note: see the plan. **Plan:** Show the open note's name in the page title. (0.2.0) |
| [2.4.3 Focus Order](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order) | Supports | Focus moves in reading order; a dialog takes focus when it opens and gives it back when it closes. |
| [2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context) | Supports | Interface links say where they go; "Learn more" links sit inside the message they belong to. |
| [2.5.1 Pointer Gestures](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-gestures) | Supports | Nothing needs a multi-point or path gesture: pinch-zoom on the canvas, the map and the graph also has buttons, the wheel or keys. |
| [2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-cancellation) | Supports | Buttons act on release (native behaviour); drags can be abandoned by moving back or pressing Escape. |
| [2.5.3 Label in Name](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name) | Partially supports | Buttons with visible text use that text as their name. Not every icon-and-text control has been checked by hand. **Plan:** A manual pass over every toolbar and dialog, recorded in the screen reader protocol. (0.2.0) |
| [2.5.4 Motion Actuation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/motion-actuation) | Not applicable | No feature uses device motion. |
| [3.1.1 Language of Page](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-page) | Supports | The page's lang attribute follows the interface language (he, en, ar, …) and dir follows it. |
| [3.2.1 On Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-focus) | Supports | Focusing a control never changes the context. |
| [3.2.2 On Input](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-input) | Supports | Changing a setting applies it in place (the theme, the language); nothing navigates away or submits on input. |
| [3.2.6 Consistent Help](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help) | Supports | Help is always in the same places: ⌘/ lists the shortcuts, and the palette has Set up Lumen…, the accessibility statement, this report and Report an accessibility problem. |
| [3.3.1 Error Identification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification) | Supports | Errors are written in text next to the field, with role="alert" (for example an invalid daily-note pattern, a bad theme file, a failed sign-in). |
| [3.3.2 Labels or Instructions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions) | Supports | Every field has a visible label or an accessible name and, where needed, an example. |
| [3.3.7 Redundant Entry](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/redundant-entry) | Supports | No process asks for the same information twice; the setup wizard keeps what was entered when you go back. |
| [4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value) | Partially supports | Native controls and ARIA widgets have names, roles and states (axe, in Hebrew and English, light and dark, on six surfaces). The canvas and the map are third-party widgets with partial roles. **Plan:** Extend the axe run to every panel and dialog, and wrap the canvas and the map in labelled regions with a keyboard summary. (0.2.0) |

## Level AA

| Criterion | Status | Remarks |
|---|---|---|
| [1.2.4 Captions (Live)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-live) | Not applicable | No live audio or video in the interface (collaboration is text only). |
| [1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-prerecorded) | Not applicable | No prerecorded video in the interface. |
| [1.3.4 Orientation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/orientation) | Supports | Works in portrait and landscape; nothing locks the orientation. |
| [1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/identify-input-purpose) | Supports | Personal-data fields use autocomplete: email, current-password and new-password in sign-in. |
| [1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum) | Supports | Text is at least 4.5:1 in light and dark mode, in all built-in themes; checked by axe in Hebrew and English. |
| [1.4.4 Resize Text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/resize-text) | Supports | Text resizes to 200 % with browser zoom without loss of content or function. |
| [1.4.5 Images of Text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/images-of-text) | Supports | The interface uses real text, never pictures of text. |
| [1.4.10 Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow) | Supports | At 320 CSS px wide (400 % zoom) the main screen, side panels and dialogs fit without horizontal scrolling. Code blocks and tables scroll inside their own box (allowed for two-dimensional content). |
| [1.4.11 Non-text Contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast) | Partially supports | Focus rings, the accent and icons meet 3:1. In the default theme the borders of some text fields are lighter than 3:1 against the background; the High contrast theme meets it everywhere. **Plan:** Darken input borders (--border-strong for fields) to 3:1 in every theme, and add the check to the contrast report. (0.2.0) |
| [1.4.12 Text Spacing](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing) | Partially supports | Layouts use flexible boxes and should take the WCAG text-spacing overrides, but this has not been tested automatically yet. **Plan:** An e2e that applies the WCAG text-spacing styles to ten surfaces and checks nothing is cut off. (0.2.0) |
| [1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus) | Partially supports | Tooltips are mostly the browser's own (title). Link previews and some popovers appear on hover; not all can be dismissed with Escape without moving the pointer. **Plan:** One popover component: dismissible with Escape, hoverable, persistent until dismissed. (0.2.0) |
| [2.4.5 Multiple Ways](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/multiple-ways) | Supports | Notes can be reached from the file tree, search, the command palette (quick open), backlinks, tags and the graph. |
| [2.4.6 Headings and Labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/headings-and-labels) | Supports | Dialogs and panels have headings; fields have labels that say what they are for. |
| [2.4.7 Focus Visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible) | Supports | Every focusable element shows a focus ring, also in forced-colours mode. |
| [2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum) | Partially supports | Dialogs are modal and centred. Notifications in the corner can sit over a focused control near the bottom edge until they go away. **Plan:** Move notifications away from the focused element, and an e2e that tabs through the main screen with notifications showing. (0.2.0) |
| [2.5.7 Dragging Movements](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements) | Partially supports | Reordering document tabs is by dragging only; there is no single-pointer or command alternative yet. Resizing the sidebar by its edge has a keyboard alternative, but not a single-pointer one. **Plan:** "Move tab left / right" in the tab's menu and the palette, and a width menu on the sidebar edge. (0.2.0) |
| [2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum) | Partially supports | Most controls are 24×24 CSS px or larger, or spaced so a 24 px circle fits. A few icon buttons in dense panels (the calendar's arrows, a toast's close button) are smaller. **Plan:** A check in the axe run for target size, and 24 px minimum for icon buttons. (0.2.0) |
| [3.1.2 Language of Parts](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-parts) | Supports | Interface text is in the interface language. Hebrew shown in an English interface (the calendar's Hebrew month names) carries lang="he". In notes, the language of each part is the author's. |
| [3.2.3 Consistent Navigation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-navigation) | Supports | The title bar, sidebar, status bar and palette are in the same place on every screen. |
| [3.2.4 Consistent Identification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-identification) | Supports | The same function has the same name and icon everywhere (commands, menus and buttons share their strings). |
| [3.3.3 Error Suggestion](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-suggestion) | Supports | Error messages say how to fix the problem ("The pattern must contain YYYY, MM and DD"). |
| [3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-prevention-legal-financial-data) | Supports | Deleting a note moves it to the trash, where it can be restored; payments happen on the payment provider's own page. |
| [3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/accessible-authentication-minimum) | Supports | Sign-in needs no cognitive test: email and password fields allow paste and password managers (autocomplete), or a single sign-on provider. |
| [4.1.3 Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages) | Supports | Notifications are in live regions that are always on the page (role="status", errors role="alert"; fixed for this report), and the editor speaks its own changes through the shared live regions. |

## Exceptions and remediation plan

Every criterion not fully supported, and what will be done about it:

- **1.1.1 Non-text Content** (A, Partially supports): Give chart and diagram blocks a text summary (title, series, values) as their accessible name, and the canvas an outline of its shapes. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.1 Use of Color** (A, Partially supports): Status-bar indicators with a visible word ("Synced", "Offline") and an accessible name, translated (their tooltips are English-only today). Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.1.1 Keyboard** (A, Partially supports): Keyboard commands to add, move and connect shapes on the canvas. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.4.2 Page Titled** (A, Supports): Show the open note's name in the page title. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.5.3 Label in Name** (A, Partially supports): A manual pass over every toolbar and dialog, recorded in the screen reader protocol. Target: 0.2.0.
- **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value** (A, Partially supports): Extend the axe run to every panel and dialog, and wrap the canvas and the map in labelled regions with a keyboard summary. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.11 Non-text Contrast** (AA, Partially supports): Darken input borders (--border-strong for fields) to 3:1 in every theme, and add the check to the contrast report. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.12 Text Spacing** (AA, Partially supports): An e2e that applies the WCAG text-spacing styles to ten surfaces and checks nothing is cut off. Target: 0.2.0.
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus** (AA, Partially supports): One popover component: dismissible with Escape, hoverable, persistent until dismissed. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)** (AA, Partially supports): Move notifications away from the focused element, and an e2e that tabs through the main screen with notifications showing. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements** (AA, Partially supports): "Move tab left / right" in the tab's menu and the palette, and a width menu on the sidebar edge. Target: 0.2.0.
- **2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)** (AA, Partially supports): A check in the axe run for target size, and 24 px minimum for icon buttons. Target: 0.2.0.

## Removed in WCAG 2.2

- 4.1.1 Parsing: Removed in WCAG 2.2 (always satisfied for HTML).

## Accessibility contact

Hit a barrier? Open an [accessibility report](https://github.com/talstilkol/lumen-md/issues/new?template=accessibility.yml) (a form labelled **accessibility**), or choose **Report an accessibility problem** in the command palette. Accessibility reports are triaged before other bugs. See also the [accessibility statement](/editor/accessibility-statement/).
